findings.statement: US unemployment rate (FRED UNRATE): 3.6% in 2019-12 (start of 2020) -> 14.8% in 2020-04 (the 2020 peak), +11.2 pts; for context, the 2018 average was 3.9%
Initial jobless claims (FRED ICSA) (level): 224,400 in 2019-11 -> 2,335,250 in 2020-03 (its best lead, 1 month earlier), a change of +2,110,850; correlation with the target r=+0.99 at a 1-month lead
Total nonfarm payrolls (FRED PAYEMS) (level): 151,794 in 2019-12 -> 130,426 in 2020-04, a change of -14.1%; correlation with the target r=-0.91 at a 0-month lead
Leisure & hospitality employment (FRED USLAH) (level): 16,805 in 2019-12 -> 8,719 in 2020-04, a change of -48.1%; correlation with the target r=-1.00 at a 0-month lead
Construction employment (FRED USCONS) (level): 7,527 in 2019-12 -> 6,522 in 2020-04, a change of -13.4%; correlation with the target r=-0.59 at a 0-month lead
Manufacturing employment (FRED MANEMP) (level): 12,760 in 2019-12 -> 11,382 in 2020-04, a change of -10.8%; correlation with the target r=-0.87 at a 0-month lead
Industrial production (FRED INDPRO) (level): 101.7 in 2019-12 -> 84.6 in 2020-04, a change of -16.9%; correlation with the target r=-0.91 at a 0-month lead
Federal funds rate (FRED FEDFUNDS) (level): 2.4% in 2019-03 -> 2.4% in 2019-07 (its best lead, 9 months earlier), a change of -0.0 pts; correlation with the target r=+0.07 at a 9-month lead
Context (Wikipedia, 'COVID-19 recession'): The recession began in most countries in February 2020.

Context (Wikipedia, 'COVID-19 recession'): After a year of global economic slowdown that saw stagnation of economic growth and consumer activity, the COVID-19 lockdowns and other precautions taken in early 2020 drove the global economy into crisis.
Context (Wikipedia, 'COVID-19 recession'): The first major sign of recession was the 2020 stock market crash, which saw major indices drop 20 to 30% in late February and March.

Context (Wikipedia, 'COVID-19 recession'): Recovery began in early April 2020; by April 2022, the GDP for most major economies had either returned to or exceeded pre-pandemic levels and many market indices recovered or even set new records by late 2020.

answer.summary: US unemployment rose in 2020: 3.6% (2019-12) -> 14.8% (2020-04 peak), +11.2 pts; 2018 average 3.9%.
